You\’ve probably heard about companies like Google and Facebook tracking you behind the scenes on third-party websites. But did you know they also track your personal information through apps on your device? Over 96\% of the 100 popular free Android apps we tested contained hidden third-party trackers. Even if you don't have a Google or Facebook account, for example, they can still collect data about you from your apps. Tracking networks like Facebook and Google use these little pieces of information to build a digital profile about you. With it, tracking networks can manipulate what you see online and allow advertisers to bid on access to you based on your data. Trackers in apps is a BIG problem for privacy. When enabled in the DuckDuckGo Privacy Browser app, App Tracking Protection blocks many trackers in other apps on your device, at the same time that the DuckDuckGo app blocks trackers we find on websites when you browse. text: How does App Tracking Protection work?
App Tracking Protection blocks known app trackers from other companies, like when Facebook tries to track you in a health app. Companies may still track you in apps they own.
Does App Tracking Protection block trackers in all my apps?

Protection may be automatically disabled for certain apps, like those that load websites, so that content appears normally. For apps with known issues, this is mostly temporary as we work to improve App Tracking Protection. You can manage this protection for each app on your device in the settings. In addition, some trackers may not be blocked because we haven't yet detected and added them to our blocklist. We are continually working to identify and protect against new trackers, so you can rest easy knowing you're getting the most up-to-date protection. You can expect updates to our tracker list every few months. These updates will get applied on your device automatically
Why does App Tracking Protection use a VPN connection?

You’ll be asked to set up a virtual private network (VPN) connection, but you don't need to install a VPN app for App Tracking Protection to work.\n\nThis permission allows App Tracking Protection, which works locally on your device, to monitor network traffic so that it can block known trackers.
Will App Tracking Protection work if I also use a VPN app?

Android only allows one active VPN connection at a time. That means you can\’t use App Tracking Protection while a VPN app on your device is running or set to “Always on.”\n\nWe recommend that you enable App Tracking Protection when you are not using a VPN app Just make sure your VPN app isn’t set to "always-on". Go to Android Network settings > VPN. Then, check the gear icon for any listed VPN apps and disable"always-on." Some VPN apps may also have an auto-connect setting which must be disabled.
How is App Tracking Protection different from a VPN?

A VPN sends your data from the device to its own server, where it secures and anonymizes your data from prying eyes. However, this allows the VPN company to see your network traffic. App Tracking Protection is different. Instead of sending your data to a VPN server, App Tracking Protection works locally on your device, sitting between your apps and the servers they talk to. Whenever App Tracking Protection recognizes a known tracker, it blocks the tracker from sending personal information (such as your IP address, activity, and device details) off your device. All other traffic reaches its destination, so your apps work normally.
App Tracking Protection works on your device and doesn’t send your personal data off your device to DuckDuckGo.

Android requires that VPNs show a persistent notification while the VPN is enabled.
